name: Frame by frame
intent: Replay one real instance of a recurring problem to find the exact moment it could have gone differently.
when: your own recurring behaviour or slip; for causes in a system, use five-whys
prompt: One real, recent time, step by step. Then find the frame where it turned.
readback: The instance must be one real occasion, not a summary of many. Check the triage: if no better option occurred to the person at that moment, it's a cue problem; if one did and they didn't want it, it's a motivation problem.

claims.claim: Reconstructing one concrete recent instance of a problem behaviour link by link, and locating the specific point where a different response was possible, identifies a better intervention point than an abstract account of the problem.
claims.construct: behavioural chain analysis; functional analysis of a single episode

claims.claim: Forming written if-then plans ("When situation X arises, I will do Y") increases goal attainment compared with forming a goal intention alone.

grounding.helps: when the same everyday slip keeps recurring and one recent instance can be recalled in detail; chain analysis is clinical craft never tested on its own, though thinking concretely about an episode is linked to less rumination than thinking about it abstractly
grounding.backfires: when the reconstruction drifts from what happened into why this always happens to you, the abstract kind of dwelling linked to rumination and low mood
